record.paper_title: Bootstrap Algebraic Multigrid: status report, open problems, and outlook
record.original_question: For non-Hermitian linear systems, which error components should restriction and interpolation approximate on coarse levels—in other words, how should algebraically smooth error be characterized when the matrix is nonnormal and the near kernel generally cannot be identified just by singular vectors or eigenvectors associated with small singular values?

evidence.quote: One main unresolved issue that arises in a Galerkin-based algebraic multigrid concerns characterizing the algebraically smooth errors that need to be approximated by restriction and interpolation.
Thus, in general the near kernel of the system matrix can not be characterized by the singular vectors (or eigenvectors) with small singular values, unless the matrix is normal.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing algebraically smooth error for nonnormal matrices in AMG remains an active research topic. Recent work (e.g., 2026 preprints on norm-based convergence bounds for nonsymmetric V-cycle AMG and optimal transfer operators for nonsymmetric two-grid methods, and a 2025 paper on near-null error components in composite adaptive AMG) provides partial answers via B-normality conditions, B-orthogonal projections, and energy-minimization frameworks induced by an HPD matrix B, but no fully general, computationally cheap characterization analogous to the Hermitian near-kernel one is established. The problem is best classified as partially solved/still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Norm-based convergence bounds for nonsymmetric algebraic V-cycle multigrid methods
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence measured in general norms induced by an HPD matrix B and B-orthogonal projections built from compatible transfer operators; introduces B-normality condition on the smoother for non-Hermitian problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides a partial framework for characterizing smooth error and convergence in nonsymmetric AMG via B-norms and B-normality.

status_evidence.title: Optimal transfer operators for nonsymmetric two-grid methods
status_evidence.snippet: Studies optimal restriction and interpolation operators specifically for nonsymmetric two-grid AMG.
status_evidence.claim: Optimal P and R for nonsymmetric problems are still being characterized in current research, indicating the underlying question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of the near-null error components utilized in composite adaptive AMG solvers
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates which near-null components are captured by adaptive AMG, including in nonsymmetric settings.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on identifying which error components must be represented on coarse levels.
